page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU is present.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3113.46, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is also strong, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 99821.78 and a passmark CPU physics test score of 7742.86, both ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, registering 138.44 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 65.88 GB/sec for large block write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25% at 23.36 GB/sec, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches an average speed of 147.36 GB/sec.

With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and a high-capacity local NVMe SSD, this server profile is highly resource-dense, offering qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and database workloads. It is well-suited for hosting relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
description: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs on an AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a 1600 GB NVMe SSD. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the processor delivers top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng benchmarks and strong multi-core capabilities. The system provides a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it highly efficient for memory-bound applications. While single-threaded compression speeds are a relative bottleneck, the server excels in multi-threaded decompression and database operations, processing 47.64 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, caching layers, and static web serving.
